title: On the field of dharma
hookLine: a teacher walks onto the field just as his two best students raise their maces at each other
carry: dharmakshetra: life is the field of dharma
tomorrow: the teacher saw the blow. what will he do?

cards: Two men face each other on open ground, each holding a heavy iron mace. One is Bhima, of the Pandava brothers. The other is Duryodhana, the Kaurava king, wet from the lake he hid in.
Just then a third man arrives, fresh from a long pilgrimage along the holy river Sarasvati. It's Balarama, Krishna's elder brother. He taught both of these men how to fight with the mace.
He has stayed out of the whole war. Now he's back in time to watch his two students try to kill each other.

teach.b: Balarama greets everyone and asks for the fight to move. In Ganguli's telling, they walk to Samantapanchaka, ground held holy, so that a warrior who dies there dies in a sacred place. It lies in Kurukshetra.
Then the cousins close in, circling like bulls. At the edge, Arjuna asks Krishna which is better. Bhima is stronger, Krishna says; Duryodhana has more practice and more skill.
Fought by the rules, Bhima may not win. Then Krishna reminds Arjuna of the dice hall, where Duryodhana bared his thigh to Draupadi, and Bhima vowed to break it.
Arjuna, where Bhima can see him, strikes his own thigh. Bhima sees.
When Duryodhana next leaps, Bhima swings low, a blow the rules of mace fighting forbid, and breaks both his thighs. The king falls. Now the teaching.
The Bhagavad Gita opens with a blind king asking about this very place: on the field of dharma, the field of the Kurus, what did my sons and Pandu's sons do? Dharmakshetra, the field of dharma.
Kurukshetra is a pilgrimage place to this day, and pilgrims bathe in its sacred tanks. And many teachers read the field inward too: later in the Gita, Krishna calls the body itself a field.
Your own life is where dharma gets kept or broken, choice by choice, even when the right blow and the forbidden one are inches apart. And the teacher of both fighters has seen all of it.

how: The mace fight between Bhima and Duryodhana is a favorite scene in retellings, dance-dramas and recitations of the Mahabharata. Kurukshetra, which takes in Samantapanchaka, is a pilgrimage place today, and pilgrims bathe in its sacred tanks such as Brahma Sarovar.

dharmakshetre kurukshetre: the blind king asks what happened on that field.

games.q: your hardest choice this week happens at a kitchen table, not a temple. by the Gita's 'field of dharma', what fits?
o: treat it as holy ground: a field where dharma gets kept or broken.
save dharma for the temple; home is just home.
wait for a bigger, more important moment.
games.why: the Gita calls the body itself a field, and teachers read every life as a Kurukshetra: the small choices count.

practice: Rest your hands on your thighs and feel the legs that carry you all day. Bring to mind the place where your hardest choices happen this week: a classroom, a kitchen table, a phone screen.
If you pray, ask God to stand with you on that field, in your own words. If you don't pray, simply call it what the Gita calls Kurukshetra, a field of dharma, and notice how you'd walk in.

wordCard.voice: Shalya. The book of the war's last day: a king out of the lake, a teacher arriving, and a vow kept with one blow below the waist.

orig.note: mace: the heavy club Bhima and Duryodhana both learned from Balarama.

carryVoice: Your line: dharmakshetra, life is the field of dharma. Tomorrow, the teacher's anger. Day eight hundred forty-seven, done.
